It wins over the property, so a client that sets `UpdateDocumentCache="false"` is not updated by `-p:ChirographUpdateOpenApiDocumentCache=true`: delete its cache file to update it. Setting the property, as above, keeps the command-line switch working for every client.

## CI without network

[Section titled “CI without network”](#ci-without-network)

Commit the cache, and either:

* leave updating on: the build tries the URL, warns with `CHIRO104`, and uses the cache. Treating warnings as errors fails such a build, so add `CHIRO104` to `WarningsNotAsErrors` (or `NoWarn`) when you do that;

* or turn updating off for CI, so the build never tries the URL:

  ```sh
  dotnet build -p:ChirographUpdateOpenApiDocumentCache=false
  ```

# Migrating from LaunchPad's preview

> The renames from the OpenAPI clients in LaunchPad's MSBuild SDK preview to Chirograph, with the behaviour that changed.

Chirograph is extracted from the OpenAPI clients of LaunchPad’s MSBuild SDK, which were never released ([LaunchPad#3238](https://github.com/RocketSurgeonsGuild/LaunchPad/pull/3238)). If you tried that preview, this page is the list of what to rename. LaunchPad’s SDK will chain Chirograph rather than carry its own copy, so a LaunchPad application gets Chirograph through LaunchPad.

## What stays the same

[Section titled “What stays the same”](#what-stays-the-same)

* The `OpenApiClient` item and all its metadata: `Generator`, `ClientName`, `Namespace`, `DocumentName`, `DocumentCache`, `UpdateDocumentCache` and `Options`.
* The three sources, and how they are inferred from `Include`.
* The configuration key, `Clients:<ClientName>:BaseAddress`.
* Where the code goes: `obj/<configuration>/<framework>/openapi/<ClientName>/`.

## Renames

[Section titled “Renames”](#renames)

Properties and the target hook lose the `LaunchPad` prefix for `Chirograph`. Diagnostic codes keep their last digits, so the search and replace is mechanical.

| LaunchPad preview                         | Chirograph                                 |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `LaunchPadUpdateOpenApiDocumentCache`     | `ChirographUpdateOpenApiDocumentCache`     |
| `LaunchPadOpenApiClientsDirectory`        | `ChirographOpenApiClientsDirectory`        |
| `LaunchPadKiotaVersion`                   | `ChirographKiotaVersion`                   |
| `LaunchPadRefitterVersion`                | `ChirographRefitterVersion`                |
| `LaunchPadKiotaBundleVersion`             | `ChirographKiotaBundleVersion`             |
| `LaunchPadRefitVersion`                   | `ChirographRefitVersion`                   |
| `LaunchPadMicrosoftExtensionsHttpVersion` | `ChirographMicrosoftExtensionsHttpVersion` |
| `LaunchPadGenerateOpenApiClients` target  | `ChirographGenerateOpenApiClients` target  |
| `LPSDK0100`                               | `CHIRO100`                                 |
| `LPSDK0101`                               | `CHIRO101`                                 |
| `LPSDK0102`                               | `CHIRO102`                                 |
| `LPSDK0103`                               | `CHIRO103`                                 |
| `LPSDK0104`                               | `CHIRO104`                                 |
| `LPSDK0105`                               | `CHIRO105`                                 |
| `LPSDK0106`                               | `CHIRO106`                                 |
| `LPSDK0107`                               | `CHIRO107`                                 |

`CHIRO107` (the generator failed) existed in the preview as `LPSDK0107`, but wasn’t documented.

## What changed

[Section titled “What changed”](#what-changed)

* **Registration.** The preview generated a joint for each client, which needed Dovetail. Chirograph generates a public `Add<ClientName>()` extension on `IServiceCollection` instead, which works without Dovetail, and with a recent Dovetail declares the joint that calls it: see [With Dovetail](../with-dovetail/).
* **`Microsoft.Extensions.Http`** is added for Kiota clients only, and not at all in a project that also has a Refitter client. `Refit.HttpClientFactory` brings its own, and the packed version could be older than that one (NU1605, a downgrade). The preview added it for both.
* **Telemetry.** The preview set environment variables Kiota doesn’t read. Chirograph sets `KIOTA_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT`, `KIOTA_OFFLINE_ENABLED` and `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT`, so Kiota’s telemetry and update check are really off.
* **`GeneratedCode`.** The registration is stamped with Chirograph’s version, not a fixed `1.0.0`.
* **A server with several target frameworks** is built as a whole and writes its document from its own outer build, rather than from its first target framework, so it works whichever frameworks the client targets.
* **`dotnet clean`** removes the generated code and the stamp that marks it up to date, so the next build generates it again.

# Migrating from OpenApiReference

> Move a project from Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Client's OpenApiReference and dotnet openapi, deprecated in .NET 10, to Chirograph's OpenApiClient.

`Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Client` gave projects the `OpenApiReference` and `OpenApiProjectReference` items, and the `dotnet openapi` command wrote them. Microsoft deprecated it in .NET 10 ([breaking change](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/compatibility/aspnet-core/10/apidescription-client-deprecated)), and now points people at each generator’s own tooling. Chirograph is that tooling for Kiota and Refitter, wired into the build the way `OpenApiReference` was.

## What changes

[Section titled “What changes”](#what-changes)

`OpenApiReference` ran NSwag (`NSwagCSharp`, `NSwagTypeScript`) by default. Chirograph runs Kiota or Refitter, which generate a different client, so the code that calls the client changes too. Pick the generator first:

* **Refitter** writes a [Refit](https://github.com/reactiveui/refit) interface with one method per operation. It is the closer of the two to NSwag’s one-class-per-API client.
* **Kiota** writes a request-builder client (`client.Rockets[id].GetAsync()`).

See [Generators](../../concepts/generators/) for the differences.

## Item by item

[Section titled “Item by item”](#item-by-item)

| `OpenApiReference`                                      | `OpenApiClient`                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Include="openapi.json"`                                | `Include="openapi.json"`, unchanged.                                           |
| `CodeGenerator="NSwagCSharp"`                           | `Generator="Refitter"` or `Generator="Kiota"`. It is required.                 |
| `ClassName="RocketsClient"`                             | `ClientName="RocketsClient"`. It is required, and also names the registration. |
| `Namespace="MyApp.Rockets"`                             | `Namespace="MyApp.Rockets"`, unchanged.                                        |
| `Options="/UseBaseUrl:false"`                           | `Options="…"`, but with the new generator’s command-line options.              |
| `OutputPath="RocketsClient.cs"`                         | None. The code always goes to `obj`, and is never committed.                   |
| `SourceUrl="https://…"` (from `dotnet openapi add url`) | `Include="https://…"` with `DocumentCache` set to the old `Include` file.      |

`OpenApiProjectReference Include="../Rockets.Api/Rockets.Api.csproj"` becomes an `OpenApiClient` whose `Include` is that project:

```xml
<OpenApiClient Include="../Rockets.Api/Rockets.Api.csproj" Generator="Refitter" ClientName="RocketsClient" />
```

## Step by step

[Section titled “Step by step”](#step-by-step)

1. Remove the `Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Client` and `NSwag.ApiDescription.Client` package references.

2. Add the Chirograph SDK to the project, as in [Getting started](../).

3. Turn each `OpenApiReference` or `OpenApiProjectReference` into an `OpenApiClient` with the table above.

4. For a URL that `dotnet openapi add url` added, keep the downloaded file and make it the cache:

   ```xml
   <!-- before -->
   <OpenApiReference Include="openapi/rockets.json" SourceUrl="https://rockets.example.com/openapi/v1.json" />


   <!-- after -->
   <OpenApiClient
     Include="https://rockets.example.com/openapi/v1.json"
     Generator="Refitter"
     ClientName="RocketsClient"
     DocumentCache="openapi/rockets.json"
   />
   ```

   `dotnet openapi refresh` is no longer needed: the build updates the cache itself, or doesn’t, as [From a URL](../from-a-url/) explains.

5. Replace the client’s construction. Where you created NSwag’s client from an `HttpClient`, register it instead and read its base address from configuration:

   ```csharp
   builder.Services.AddRocketsClient();
   ```

   ```json
   { "Clients": { "RocketsClient": { "BaseAddress": "https://rockets.example.com/" } } }
   ```

6. Update the call sites to the new client’s methods.

# With Dovetail

> Chirograph declares a Dovetail joint for every client through DovetailTemplate, so a host built with ConfigureDovetail() resolves it with no registration call.

[Dovetail](https://rocketsurgeonsguild.github.io/Dovetail/) registers services through joints: classes the host finds at build time and runs when `ConfigureDovetail()` builds it. Chirograph never references Dovetail. Every client gets a plain [`Add<ClientName>()` registration](../../concepts/registration/), and a joint is one more caller of it.

## The joint Chirograph declares

[Section titled “The joint Chirograph declares”](#the-joint-chirograph-declares)

Note

This needs **Dovetail 0.6.0** or later: the first release in which `DovetailTemplate` replaces every metadata value as a token ([Dovetail#413](https://github.com/RocketSurgeonsGuild/Dovetail/issues/413)). With an older Dovetail, Chirograph declares nothing, the build still succeeds, and you register the client [yourself](#a-joint-of-your-own).

Dovetail has an extension point for packages that ship C#: a [`DovetailTemplate`](https://rocketsurgeonsguild.github.io/Dovetail/reference/dovetail-template/) item, which Dovetail expands into a file only in projects that run its source generator. Chirograph declares one per client. For the client `RocketsClient` in `MyApp.Rockets` it is:

```xml
<DovetailTemplate Include="Chirograph.RocketsClient"
                  File="…/Sdk/templates/OpenApiClientJoint.cs.template"
                  ClientName="RocketsClient"
                  Namespace="MyApp.Rockets"
                  ChirographVersion="…" />
```

Dovetail writes it as `obj/…/DovetailTemplate.Chirograph.RocketsClient.g.cs`, with each `__Name__` token replaced by the metadata of the same name:

```csharp
namespace MyApp.Rockets;


[DovetailExport]
internal sealed class RocketsClientJoint : IServiceJoint
{
    public void Register(IDovetailContext context, IServiceCollection services) =>
        global::MyApp.Rockets.RocketsClientServiceCollectionExtensions.AddRocketsClient(services);
}
```

So the client resolves from a host built with `ConfigureDovetail()`, with no registration call of your own:

```csharp
using var host = await Host.CreateApplicationBuilder(args).ConfigureDovetail();
var client = host.Services.GetRequiredService<RocketsClient>();
```

* The items are declared only when the Dovetail in the build sets `DovetailTemplateMetadataTokens`, the capability property that release added. An older Dovetail never gets a template it can’t expand.
* The `Include` is prefixed with `Chirograph.`, so it can’t clash with another package’s template for a type of the same name.
* Dovetail writes the joint only into a project that runs its source generator. A library that generates a client and references Dovetail exports the joint to every application that references it, as any exported joint is.
* `ChirographGenerateDovetailJoint=false` turns the joints off for the project. See [Properties](../../reference/properties/).

## A joint of your own

[Section titled “A joint of your own”](#a-joint-of-your-own)

Turn the generated joints off and write your own when you want to configure the client further, on the builder the registration returns, or when your Dovetail is older than the release above:

```csharp
[DovetailExport]
public sealed class RocketsClientSetup : IServiceJoint
{
    public void Register(IDovetailContext context, IServiceCollection services) =>
        services.AddRocketsClient().AddStandardResilienceHandler();
}
```

`AddStandardResilienceHandler()` comes from `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience`, as an example of chaining on the `IHttpClientBuilder`. Don’t name your joint `<ClientName>Joint` in the client’s namespace while the generated joints are on: that is the name of the generated one.

# With Optionary

> Chirograph declares the schema of each client's Clients:<ClientName> section to Optionary, so appsettings.json gets IntelliSense and validation for it.

[Optionary](https://rocketsurgeonsguild.github.io/Optionary/) writes an `appsettings.schema.json` for an application from the configuration sections it and its references declare. Chirograph declares each client’s section, `Clients:<ClientName>`, so an application that references Optionary gets completion and validation for its clients in `appsettings.json`. Chirograph never references Optionary, and the registration still reads the section from `IConfiguration` without it.

## Turning it on

[Section titled “Turning it on”](#turning-it-on)

Reference Optionary in the project that declares the clients:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="Optionary" Version="…" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Note

This needs Optionary 0.1.0 or later, the first release that reads the `OptionarySchemaFragment` item. With an older Optionary, or none, the item is ignored and the build still succeeds.

Build, and the application’s `obj/appsettings.schema.json` (copied next to the application) holds a `Clients` section with one entry per client. A library that declares the clients puts them in its own schema instead, and every application that references it merges them, as Optionary does for any section.

## The keys

[Section titled “The keys”](#the-keys)

The registration reads the whole section (see [Registration](../../concepts/registration/)). The schema describes:

| Key                     | Type                                                                                                                                                                | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ConnectionString`      | string                                                                                                                                                              | The client’s connection string. It wins over the other keys, and set (even empty), `ConnectionStrings:<ClientName>` is not read.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `BaseAddress`           | absolute URI                                                                                                                                                        | The `HttpClient.BaseAddress`. A Refitter client needs one, here or in a connection string; a Kiota client falls back to its document’s first server.                                                                                                                                           |
| `Endpoint`              | absolute URI                                                                                                                                                        | An alias of `BaseAddress`. Set one or the other, not both.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Timeout`               | TimeSpan, `hh:mm:ss`                                                                                                                                                | The `HttpClient.Timeout`, written as `IConfiguration` binds a `TimeSpan`, such as `00:00:30`.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `DefaultRequestHeaders` | object of string values                                                                                                                                             | Headers sent with every request, each name with its value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Resilience`            | boolean, or an object when the project references `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience`                                                                            | `true` adds the standard resilience handler; an object sets its [settings](../../concepts/registration/#resilience) (`Retry`, `CircuitBreaker`, `AttemptTimeout`, `TotalRequestTimeout`, `RateLimiter`). Only takes effect when the project references `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience`. |
| `AllowedHosts`          | array of strings                                                                                                                                                    | More hosts than the `BaseAddress` host that may receive the client’s credentials: a host alone allows each of its ports, `host:port` that port.                                                                                                                                                |
| `Authentication`        | `None`, `ApiKey`, `Bearer`, `Basic`, `ClientCredentials`, `PrivateKeyJwt`, `AzureDefault`, `AzureManagedIdentity`, `AzureWorkloadIdentity`, `AzureServicePrincipal` | How the client authenticates. `None`, the default, takes the authentication from the container. `ClientCredentials`, `PrivateKeyJwt` and the Azure methods need the item’s metadata.                                                                                                           |
| `ApiKey`                | string                                                                                                                                                              | The key of `ApiKey`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Key`                   | string                                                                                                                                                              | An alias of `ApiKey`. Set one or the other, not both.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ApiKeyHeader`          | string                                                                                                                                                              | The header `ApiKey` sends the key in, `X-Api-Key` by default.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ApiKeyQuery`           | string                                                                                                                                                              | The query parameter `ApiKey` sends the key in, instead of a header.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `Token`                 | string                                                                                                                                                              | The token of `Bearer`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Username`              | string                                                                                                                                                              | The user name of `Basic`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Password`              | string                                                                                                                                                              | The password of `Basic`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `CertificatePath`       | string                                                                                                                                                              | A client certificate, for mutual TLS or for `PrivateKeyJwt` or `AzureServicePrincipal` to sign with: a PKCS#12 (`.pfx`, `.p12`) or PEM file. Not with `CertificateThumbprint`.                                                                                                                 |
| `CertificatePassword`   | string                                                                                                                                                              | The password of the PKCS#12 file, or of its encrypted PEM key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `CertificateKeyPath`    | string                                                                                                                                                              | The PEM private key, when `CertificatePath` is a PEM certificate without its key.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `CertificateThumbprint` | string                                                                                                                                                              | A client certificate in `CertificateStore`, instead of a file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `CertificateStore`      | `<location>/<name>`                                                                                                                                                 | The store of `CertificateThumbprint`: `CurrentUser/My` (the default) or `LocalMachine/My`, say.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ClientId`              | string                                                                                                                                                              | The client id of `ClientCredentials` and `PrivateKeyJwt`, or of the application or user-assigned identity of an Azure method.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ClientSecret`          | string                                                                                                                                                              | The client secret of `ClientCredentials` or `AzureServicePrincipal`, not of `PrivateKeyJwt`. Keep it out of `appsettings.json`.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `Scope`                 | string                                                                                                                                                              | The scopes a token is asked for, space-separated: optional for `ClientCredentials` and `PrivateKeyJwt`, needed by an Azure method.                                                                                                                                                             |
| `TokenEndpoint`         | absolute URI                                                                                                                                                        | The token endpoint of `ClientCredentials` and `PrivateKeyJwt`. Not with `Authority`.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Authority`             | absolute https URI                                                                                                                                                  | The authority whose discovery document gives the token endpoint of `ClientCredentials` and `PrivateKeyJwt`. Not with `TokenEndpoint`.                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Resource`              | string                                                                                                                                                              | The resource `ClientCredentials` and `PrivateKeyJwt` ask for.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ClientCredentialStyle` | `Header`, `Body`                                                                                                                                                    | How `ClientCredentials` sends the client id and secret.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `TenantId`              | string                                                                                                                                                              | The tenant of an Azure method, its id or a domain.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

```json
{
    "Clients": {
        "RocketsClient": {
            "BaseAddress": "https://rockets.example.com/",
            "Timeout": "00:00:30",
            "DefaultRequestHeaders": { "X-Api-Key": "…" },
            "Resilience": true
        }
    }
}
```

## The rules

[Section titled “The rules”](#the-rules)

Beyond the keys, the schema checks what a validator can see in `appsettings.json`:

* `Authentication` takes only the methods the client allows: `None`, `ApiKey`, `Bearer` and `Basic`.
* When `Authentication` names a method, the keys of the other methods are not allowed, and the keys the method needs are required (`Username` for `Basic`). A secret is never required, since it belongs elsewhere.
* A section without `Authentication` is not checked against the methods: a connection string can name the method.
* The secrets (`ApiKey`, `Key`, `Token`, `Password`, `CertificatePassword`) say in their description to keep them out of `appsettings.json`, in user secrets, an environment variable or a vault.
* `ConnectionString` is a plain string: a schema cannot check what is inside it. `ConnectionStrings:<ClientName>` is not described, since Optionary describes the sections the application owns.
* Neither generator requires `BaseAddress`: a connection string, in the section or in `ConnectionStrings:<ClientName>`, can give it, and with service discovery the client has a default address. With service discovery, the description of `BaseAddress` says it may be a service-discovery address, and gives its default, `https+http://<ClientName>`.

## What Chirograph declares

[Section titled “What Chirograph declares”](#what-chirograph-declares)

For each client with a valid `ClientName`, Chirograph writes the client’s schema when the project builds (a design-time build too), into the client’s folder, and adds an `OptionarySchemaFragment` item at evaluation whose `File` is that schema:

```xml
<OptionarySchemaFragment Include="Clients:RocketsClient" File="obj/Debug/net10.0/openapi/RocketsClient/RocketsClient.schema.json" />
<OptionarySchemaFragment Include="Clients:RocketsRefitClient" File="obj/Debug/net10.0/openapi/RocketsRefitClient/RocketsRefitClient.schema.json" />
```

The schema is the client’s own: its descriptions name the client and its generator, and its `Authentication` lists the methods the client allows. Optionary merges a section that several items or options types declare, so your own fragment for `Clients:RocketsClient` adds to Chirograph’s.

`ChirographOptionarySchema=false` turns the items and the schemas off for the project. See [Properties](../../reference/properties/).

# Reference

> The OpenApiClient item, the properties and target hooks, the diagnostic codes and the generated code.

Everything here is public API under semantic versioning: the item and its metadata, the properties, the target hooks, the diagnostic codes and the shape of the generated registration. Names that start with `_Chirograph` are private and can change in any release.

* [`OpenApiClient`](openapiclient/): the item, and every metadata value it reads.
* [Properties](properties/): the properties that change every client of a project, and the target hooks.
* [Diagnostics](diagnostics/): each error and warning, what causes it and how to fix it. Each code has its own anchor, which the build message links to.
* [Generated code](generated-code/): the files in each client’s folder, and the registration.

A test in the repository reads the SDK’s targets and fails when these pages list different metadata, properties or codes from the ones the targets read and raise.

# Diagnostics

> Every error and warning Chirograph raises, CHIRO100 to CHIRO109, with the message, the cause and the fix.

Each diagnostic links here from the build output: an IDE shows the code as a link to its heading below. A release of Chirograph links to this page in the docs of that release, and a prerelease to the latest docs. Codes keep their last digits from LaunchPad’s preview (`LPSDK0100` is `CHIRO100`); see [Migrating from LaunchPad’s preview](../../guides/migrating-from-launchpad/).

## Codes

[Section titled “Codes”](#codes)

| Code                    | Severity | Meaning                                                                     |
| ----------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`CHIRO100`](#chiro100) | error    | `Generator` is missing or is not `Kiota` or `Refitter`.                     |
| [`CHIRO101`](#chiro101) | error    | `ClientName` is missing or is not a C# identifier.                          |
| [`CHIRO102`](#chiro102) | error    | The document file does not exist.                                           |
| [`CHIRO103`](#chiro103) | error    | The server project wrote several documents, or none matched `DocumentName`. |
| [`CHIRO104`](#chiro104) | warning  | The URL could not be reached. The cached document is used.                  |
| [`CHIRO105`](#chiro105) | error    | The URL could not be reached, and there is no cached document.              |
| [`CHIRO106`](#chiro106) | error    | The generator tool is not in the packages folders. Restore the project.     |
| [`CHIRO107`](#chiro107) | error    | The generator exited with an error. Its output is included.                 |
| [`CHIRO108`](#chiro108) | error    | Two clients have the same `ClientName`.                                     |
| [`CHIRO109`](#chiro109) | error    | `Authentication` lists a value Chirograph doesn’t know.                     |

## CHIRO100

[Section titled “CHIRO100”](#chiro100)

> The OpenApiClient ‘openapi/rockets.json’ has Generator ‘NSwag’: set it to Kiota or Refitter.

The item’s `Generator` is empty, or names a generator Chirograph doesn’t run. The comparison is case-sensitive. Set it to `Kiota` or `Refitter`; see [Generators](../../concepts/generators/) to choose.

## CHIRO101

[Section titled “CHIRO101”](#chiro101)

> The OpenApiClient ‘openapi/rockets.json’ has ClientName ‘Rockets.Client’: set it to the name of the client, a C# identifier.

`ClientName` is empty, or is not a C# identifier: letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit. It names a class, an interface, a method and a configuration key, so it can’t contain dots or dashes. Put the namespace in `Namespace` instead.

## CHIRO102

[Section titled “CHIRO102”](#chiro102)

> The OpenAPI document ‘openapi/rockets.json’ of the OpenApiClient ‘RocketsClient’ does not exist.

A [file source](../../guides/from-a-file/) points at a file that isn’t there. The path is relative to the project, not to the solution or the current folder. An `Include` meant as a URL has to start with `http://` or `https://`.

## CHIRO103

[Section titled “CHIRO103”](#chiro103)

> The project ’../Rockets.Api/Rockets.Api.csproj’ of the OpenApiClient ‘RocketsClient’ wrote the documents ’…/Rockets.Api.json;…/Rockets.Api_v2.json’: set DocumentName to the one the client is generated from.

A [server project](../../guides/from-a-server-project/) wrote more than one document and the client has no `DocumentName`, or none of the documents matches `DocumentName`. The message lists what the server wrote. `<Project>.json` is `v1`, and `<Project>_<name>.json` is `<name>`. When the list is empty, the server wrote no document: check that it references `Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server` and calls `AddOpenApi()`.

## CHIRO104

[Section titled “CHIRO104”](#chiro104)

> The OpenAPI document of the OpenApiClient ‘RocketsClient’ could not be downloaded from ‘<https://rockets.example.com/openapi/v1.json>’: the client is generated from the cached copy, ’…/openapi/rockets.json’.

A warning. The [URL](../../guides/from-a-url/) couldn’t be downloaded, so the client is generated from the [document cache](../../concepts/document-cache/). The build succeeds with the last document it saw. Fix the URL or the network, or turn updating off so the build doesn’t try (`ChirographUpdateOpenApiDocumentCache=false`). A build that treats warnings as errors fails on it unless `CHIRO104` is in `WarningsNotAsErrors`.

## CHIRO105

[Section titled “CHIRO105”](#chiro105)

> The OpenAPI document of the OpenApiClient ‘RocketsClient’ could not be downloaded from ‘<https://rockets.example.com/openapi/v1.json>’, and there is no cached copy.

The URL couldn’t be downloaded, and there is nothing to fall back on: a fresh clone or a clean agent with a cache in `obj`. Build once where the URL can be reached, or set `DocumentCache` to a file in the project and commit it.

## CHIRO106

[Section titled “CHIRO106”](#chiro106)

> The Kiota tool the OpenApiClient ‘RocketsClient’ is generated with was not found in the packages folders (…): restore the project.

The generator’s tool package isn’t in any of the packages folders restore uses. Restore the project (`dotnet restore`, or a build without `--no-restore`). After changing `ChirographKiotaVersion` or `ChirographRefitterVersion`, the new version has to be restored too, and has to exist on your package sources.

## CHIRO107

[Section titled “CHIRO107”](#chiro107)

> Kiota could not generate the OpenAPI client RocketsClient (exit code 1): …

The generator ran and failed. The message ends with everything it wrote. The usual causes are a document that isn’t valid OpenAPI, or an `Options` value the generator doesn’t accept. Run the generator by hand on the client’s copy of the document, in `obj/<configuration>/<framework>/openapi/<ClientName>/`, to see the problem outside the build.

## CHIRO108

[Section titled “CHIRO108”](#chiro108)

> The OpenApiClient items ‘openapi/rockets.json, openapi/rockets-v2.json’ have the same ClientName ‘RocketsClient’: give each client a name of its own.

Two `OpenApiClient` items in one project have the same `ClientName`. They would be generated into the same folder, with the same types and the same `Add<ClientName>()`, so the build stops before it generates either. Give each client its own `ClientName`; two clients can still be generated from the same document.

## CHIRO109

[Section titled “CHIRO109”](#chiro109)

> The OpenApiClient ‘RocketsClient’ has Authentication values Chirograph doesn’t know (Bearer, Kerberos): set it to a ;-separated list of ClientCredentials, Azure, or leave it out.

The item’s `Authentication` metadata lists the methods that need a package, which the item must declare: `ClientCredentials` (which allows `PrivateKeyJwt` too) and `Azure` (the four Azure methods). The comparison ignores case. `None`, `ApiKey`, `Bearer` and `Basic` need no package and are always available, so they don’t go in the metadata: configuration chooses among them with `Clients:<ClientName>:Authentication`. Remove the unknown values; see [Authentication](../openapiclient/#metadata).

# Generated code

> The files Chirograph writes for each client in obj, which of them are compiled, and the shape of the generated Add<ClientName>() registration and <ClientName>Options.

For a client `RocketsClient` in namespace `MyApp.Rockets`, everything is in `obj/<configuration>/<framework>/openapi/RocketsClient/` (the parent folder is `ChirographOpenApiClientsDirectory`). Nothing is written into the project, and nothing there is meant to be committed.

## The folder

[Section titled “The folder”](#the-folder)

| File                                            | What it is                                                                                                                                                                               | Compiled |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `generated/**`                                  | The generator’s output. Kiota: the `RocketsClient` class, its request builders and models, and `kiota-lock.json`. Refitter: `RocketsClient.cs`, with `IRocketsClient` and its contracts. | `*.cs`   |
| `RocketsClientServiceCollectionExtensions.g.cs` | The [registration](#the-registration).                                                                                                                                                   | yes      |
| `RocketsClientOptions.g.cs`                     | The [options](#the-options) the registration reads, with their connection-string parser and validation.                                                                                  | yes      |
| `RocketsClient.schema.json`                     | The schema of the client’s `Clients:RocketsClient` section, for [Optionary](../../guides/with-optionary/). Not written with `ChirographOptionarySchema=false`.                           | no       |
| `openapi.json`, `openapi.yaml` or `openapi.yml` | The client’s copy of its document, written only when the content changes.                                                                                                                | no       |
| `settings.txt`                                  | The generator, its version, `ClientName`, `Namespace` and `Options`, written only when they change.                                                                                      | no       |
| `generated.stamp`                               | Touched after each generation. The generator runs again when the document’s copy or `settings.txt` is newer.                                                                             | no       |
| `RocketsClient.refitter`                        | Refitter only: the settings file Refitter runs with.                                                                                                                                     | no       |
| `download/`                                     | URL only: the last download, before it is compared with the cache.                                                                                                                       | no       |

Every file here is added to `FileWrites`, so `dotnet clean` removes them all, `generated.stamp` included, and the next build generates the client again. A `DocumentCache` in the project is not in this folder, and a clean leaves it alone.

## The registration

[Section titled “The registration”](#the-registration)

Kiota’s registration:

```csharp
namespace MyApp.Rockets;


[GeneratedCode("Chirograph", "1.0.0")]
public static class RocketsClientServiceCollectionExtensions
{
    internal const string SectionKey = "Clients:RocketsClient";
    internal const string ConnectionStringKey = SectionKey + ":ConnectionString";


    public static IHttpClientBuilder AddRocketsClient(this IServiceCollection services, Action<RocketsClientOptions>? configure = null)
    {
        // the options: keys, then code, then the connection string; validated at startup
        RocketsClientOptionsSetup.Register(services);
        if (configure is not null) services.Configure(configure);


        var builder = services.AddHttpClient("RocketsClient");
        builder.ConfigureHttpClient((provider, httpClient) =>
        {
            var options = Options(provider);
            if (options.BaseAddress is { Length: > 0 } baseAddress)
                httpClient.BaseAddress = new Uri(baseAddress, UriKind.Absolute);
            if (options.Timeout is { } timeout)
                httpClient.Timeout = timeout;
            foreach (var header in options.DefaultRequestHeaders)
                httpClient.DefaultRequestHeaders.TryAddWithoutValidation(header.Key, header.Value);
        });
        // the client certificate (mTLS), on the primary handler the factory made
        builder.ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler((handler, provider) => RocketsClientCertificate.Present(handler, Options(provider)));
        builder.AddTypedClient<RocketsClient>((httpClient, services) =>
        {
            // keyed with "RocketsClient", else unkeyed, else none (anonymous for the authentication provider, and with an
            // Authentication configured, whose handler sets the credentials)
            var options = Options(services);
            var adapter = new HttpClientRequestAdapter(
                (options.Authentication == RocketsClientAuthentication.None ? Resolve<IAuthenticationProvider>(services) : null)
                    ?? new AnonymousAuthenticationProvider(),
                Resolve<IParseNodeFactory>(services),
                Resolve<ISerializationWriterFactory>(services),
                httpClient);
            var configureRequestAdapter = options.ConfigureRequestAdapter;
            return new RocketsClient(configureRequestAdapter is null ? adapter : configureRequestAdapter(services, adapter));
        });
        // when Authentication isn't None, the handler that adds the credentials, after the handlers added so far: Prepare makes it
        // and takes over the redirects of the primary handler, Add adds it
        builder.ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler((handler, provider) => RocketsClientAuthenticationHandler.Prepare(handler, provider));
        builder.ConfigureAdditionalHttpMessageHandlers((handlers, _) => RocketsClientAuthenticationHandler.Add(handlers));
        return builder;
    }


    // read when the HttpClient is created, so a configuration reload applies
    private static RocketsClientOptions Options(IServiceProvider services) =>
        services.GetRequiredService<IOptionsMonitor<RocketsClientOptions>>().CurrentValue;
}
```

When the project references Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience, the build writes this before the authentication handler too, and leaves it out otherwise:

```csharp
builder.AddStandardResilienceHandler();
builder.ConfigureAdditionalHttpMessageHandlers((handlers, provider) =>
{
    var resilience = Options(provider).Resilience;
    // the handler added just above is the last one so far
    if (!resilience && handlers.Count > 0 && handlers[^1] is ResilienceHandler)
        handlers.RemoveAt(handlers.Count - 1);
});
```

When the project references Microsoft.Extensions.ServiceDiscovery, the build writes this after the authentication handler, and leaves it out otherwise. The options then default `BaseAddress` to `https+http://RocketsClient`, accept a service-discovery address, and fail validation at startup when the application registered no service-discovery provider (it calls `services.AddServiceDiscovery()`):

```csharp
builder.AddServiceDiscovery();
```

See [Configuration](../../concepts/registration/#configuration) for what each key does.

Refitter’s is the same, except that it registers the Refit interface instead of a named client:

```csharp
var builder = services.AddRefitGeneratedClient<IRocketsClient>(static provider =>
{
    var settings = Resolve<RefitSettings>(provider);
    var configureRefitSettings = Options(provider).ConfigureRefitSettings;
    return configureRefitSettings is null ? settings : configureRefitSettings(provider, settings);
});
```

The real files spell every type with `global::` and call the extension methods as static methods, so they compile whatever the project’s usings are. The `GeneratedCode` version is the version of Chirograph that wrote the file.

The class name, the method name and its parameters and the return type are public API. The `SectionKey` and `ConnectionStringKey` constants are internal, for the project’s own code. The body can change between releases.

## The options

[Section titled “The options”](#the-options)

`RocketsClientOptions.g.cs` holds the client’s options and what fills them:

* `RocketsClientOptions`, public: `BaseAddress`, `Timeout`, `DefaultRequestHeaders`, `Resilience`, `AllowedHosts`, `Authentication` and the keys of its methods (`ApiKey`, `ApiKeyHeader`, `ApiKeyQuery`, `Token`, `TokenProvider`, `Username`, `Password`), the certificate keys (`CertificatePath`, `CertificatePassword`, `CertificateKeyPath`, `CertificateThumbprint`, `CertificateStore`), plus `ConfigureRequestAdapter` (Kiota) or `ConfigureRefitSettings` (Refitter).
* `RocketsClientAuthentication`, public: the methods the client can be configured with, `None`, `ApiKey`, `Bearer` and `Basic`.
* `RocketsClientOptionsSetup`, internal: it fills the options from the keys under `Clients:RocketsClient` (an `IConfigureOptions`) and from the connection string (an `IPostConfigureOptions`), validates them (an `IValidateOptions`), and reloads them with the configuration (an `IOptionsChangeTokenSource`). It parses the connection string itself, without `DbConnectionStringBuilder` or the configuration binder, so nothing in it needs reflection.
* `RocketsClientAuthenticationHandler`, internal: the `DelegatingHandler` that adds the configured credentials to the requests for the allowed hosts, and follows redirects in place of the primary handler (see [Configured authentication](../../concepts/registration/#configured-authentication)).
* `RocketsClientCertificate`, internal: it loads the certificate the certificate keys give (a PKCS#12 or PEM file, or a store), checks those keys, and sets the certificate on the primary handler for mutual TLS.

With `Authentication="ClientCredentials"` on the item, and only then, the file also has:

* `ClientCredentials` and `PrivateKeyJwt` in `RocketsClientAuthentication`, and their keys on `RocketsClientOptions`: `ClientId`, `ClientSecret`, `Scope`, `TokenEndpoint`, `Authority`, `Resource` and `ClientCredentialStyle`.
* `RocketsClientCredentialStyle`, public: `Header` or `Body`.
* `RocketsClientClientCredentials`, internal: it configures Duende’s client-credentials client `RocketsClient` from the options, reads the token endpoint from the `Authority`’s discovery document, and gives the handler the token (see [Client credentials](../../concepts/registration/#client-credentials)). The registration calls Duende’s `AddClientCredentialsTokenManagement()`.
* `RocketsClientClientAssertion`, internal: the `IClientAssertionService` keyed `"RocketsClient"`, which signs the assertion of `PrivateKeyJwt` with the certificate, and `RocketsClientClientAssertions`, internal: the unkeyed `IClientAssertionService` Duende asks, which hands each client to the one keyed with its name (see [Private key JWT](../../concepts/registration/#private-key-jwt)).

With `Authentication="Azure"` on the item, and only then, the file also has:

* `AzureDefault`, `AzureManagedIdentity`, `AzureWorkloadIdentity` and `AzureServicePrincipal` in `RocketsClientAuthentication`, and their keys on `RocketsClientOptions`: `ClientId`, `ClientSecret`, `Scope` (shared with `ClientCredentials`) and `TenantId`.
* `RocketsClientAzureCredential`, internal: it makes the client’s Azure.Identity credential from the options (or takes the `TokenCredential` registered keyed `"RocketsClient"`), checks the keys, and gives the handler the token (see [Azure](../../concepts/registration/#azure)).

The public types and their members are public API. See [The options](../../concepts/registration/#the-options) for the order of the sources and [Validation](../../concepts/registration/#validation) for what fails.

## The Dovetail joint

[Section titled “The Dovetail joint”](#the-dovetail-joint)

With a Dovetail that can expand it, Dovetail (not Chirograph) also writes a joint for each client, outside the client’s folder: `obj/<configuration>/<framework>/DovetailTemplate.Chirograph.RocketsClient.g.cs`. It is an internal `[DovetailExport]` class, `RocketsClientJoint`, in the client’s namespace, whose `Register` calls `AddRocketsClient(services)`. Its name is all of it that is API. See [With Dovetail](../../guides/with-dovetail/).

# OpenApiClient

> The OpenApiClient MSBuild item declares one client. Every metadata value it reads, whether it is required, its default and what it changes.

An `OpenApiClient` item declares one client: a document, the generator that turns it into code, and the name of what is generated.

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <OpenApiClient Include="openapi/rockets.yaml" Generator="Refitter" ClientName="RocketsClient" Namespace="MyApp.Rockets" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Declare it in the project file, or in a `Directory.Build.targets`. The SDK reads the items when the project is evaluated (to add packages, tool downloads and server references) and again when it builds.

## Metadata

[Section titled “Metadata”](#metadata)

Metadata the item doesn’t read is ignored without a warning, so a misspelt name falls back to its default.

| Metadata              | Required | Default                                                    | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Include`             | yes      |                                                            | The [source](../../concepts/sources/). A `.csproj`, `.fsproj` or `.vbproj` is a server project. `http://` or `https://` is a URL. Anything else is a file (`.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml`), relative to the project.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Generator`           | yes      |                                                            | `Kiota` or `Refitter` ([`CHIRO100`](../diagnostics/#chiro100)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ClientName`          | yes      |                                                            | A C# identifier ([`CHIRO101`](../diagnostics/#chiro101)), unique within the project ([`CHIRO108`](../diagnostics/#chiro108)). Kiota’s client class is called this, Refitter’s interface is `I<ClientName>`, the registration is `Add<ClientName>()` and its configuration section is `Clients:<ClientName>`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Namespace`           | no       | `$(RootNamespace)`                                         | The namespace of everything generated for the client. Give each client its own when a project has several.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `DocumentName`        | no       | the only document                                          | Server project only: the document to generate from, when the server writes several. `v1` is ASP.NET Core’s default ([`CHIRO103`](../diagnostics/#chiro103)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `DocumentCache`       | no       | the document’s copy in `obj`                               | URL only: a file, relative to the project, to keep the last download in. Commit it to build without the URL. See [Document cache](../../concepts/document-cache/).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `UpdateDocumentCache` | no       | `$(ChirographUpdateOpenApiDocumentCache)`, which is `true` | URL only: `false` uses the cache whenever it exists instead of downloading. Wins over the property.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Options`             | no       |                                                            | More arguments for the generator: after `kiota generate …`, or after Refitter’s settings file. See [Generators](../../concepts/generators/#what-chirograph-passes).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Authentication`      | no       |                                                            | A `;`-separated list of the authentication methods the client may use beyond `None`, `ApiKey`, `Bearer` and `Basic`: `ClientCredentials`, which adds `Duende.AccessTokenManagement` and allows `ClientCredentials` and `PrivateKeyJwt`, and `Azure`, which adds `Azure.Identity` and allows `AzureDefault`, `AzureManagedIdentity`, `AzureWorkloadIdentity` and `AzureServicePrincipal`. An unknown value is [`CHIRO109`](../diagnostics/#chiro109). See [Client credentials](../../concepts/registration/#client-credentials), [Private key JWT](../../concepts/registration/#private-key-jwt) and [Azure](../../concepts/registration/#azure). |

`DocumentName` is ignored for a file or URL, and `DocumentCache` and `UpdateDocumentCache` for a file or server project.

## What changes when

[Section titled “What changes when”](#what-changes-when)

* Changing `Generator`, `ClientName`, `Namespace` or `Options` generates the client again on the next build. Changing `Authentication` only rewrites the registration and the options.
* Changing `Include` to another document of the same content changes nothing: the client is generated from the content, not the path.
* Removing an item leaves its folder in `obj`, but its code is no longer compiled.

# Properties

> The MSBuild properties that change every client of a project, their defaults, and the target hooks before and after generation.

Set a property in the project file, a `Directory.Build.props`, or on the command line (`-p:Name=value`). The version properties are set when the SDK is imported, each only when the project hasn’t set it already, so a value in `Directory.Build.props` or the project wins.

## Properties

[Section titled “Properties”](#properties)

| Property                                       | Default                             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ChirographUpdateOpenApiDocumentCache`         | `true`                              | The default of every client’s `UpdateDocumentCache`: whether a URL is downloaded again when its document is cached. See [Document cache](../../concepts/document-cache/#updating).         |
| `ChirographGenerateDovetailJoint`              | `true`                              | Whether each client gets a Dovetail joint, with a Dovetail that can write it. See [With Dovetail](../../guides/with-dovetail/).                                                            |
| `ChirographOptionarySchema`                    | `true`                              | Whether each client declares the schema of its `Clients:<ClientName>` section to Optionary. See [With Optionary](../../guides/with-optionary/).                                            |
| `ChirographOpenApiClientsDirectory`            | `$(IntermediateOutputPath)openapi/` | The folder each client’s folder goes in, relative to the project. A folder inside the project is left out of its default items, so the code is compiled once.                              |
| `ChirographKiotaVersion`                       | the packed version                  | The version of the `Microsoft.OpenApi.Kiota` tool.                                                                                                                                         |
| `ChirographRefitterVersion`                    | the packed version                  | The version of the `Refitter` tool.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `ChirographKiotaBundleVersion`                 | the packed version                  | The version of `Microsoft.Kiota.Bundle` added to a project with a Kiota client.                                                                                                            |
| `ChirographRefitVersion`                       | the packed version                  | The version of `Refit.HttpClientFactory` added to a project with a Refitter client.                                                                                                        |
| `ChirographMicrosoftExtensionsHttpVersion`     | the packed version                  | The version of `Microsoft.Extensions.Http` added to a project with a Kiota client and no Refitter client.                                                                                  |
| `ChirographDuendeAccessTokenManagementVersion` | the packed version                  | The version of `Duende.AccessTokenManagement` added to a project with a client whose `Authentication` declares `ClientCredentials`. Only 4.x works with the generated code.                |
| `ChirographAzureIdentityVersion`               | the packed version                  | The version of `Azure.Identity` added to a project with a client whose `Authentication` declares `Azure`.                                                                                  |
| `ChirographVersion`                            | the SDK’s version                   | Stamped into the registration’s `[GeneratedCode]`. Read it; don’t set it.                                                                                                                  |
| `ChirographGenerateOpenApiClientsDependsOn`    | empty                               | Targets to run before the documents are read, after `ChirographBeforeGenerateOpenApiClients`. Add yours: `$(ChirographGenerateOpenApiClientsDependsOn);MyTarget`. See [Targets](#targets). |

The packed versions are the ones Chirograph’s own repository pinned when the SDK was packed: they are in the package’s `Sdk/Packages.props`. A package the project references itself is never added, whatever these say: see [Generators](../../concepts/generators/#the-packages-added-to-the-project).

A tool version that isn’t in the packages folder fails the build with [`CHIRO106`](../diagnostics/#chiro106) until the project is restored.

## Targets

[Section titled “Targets”](#targets)

| Target                                   | Runs                                                                            | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ChirographGenerateOpenApiClients`       | after `ResolveProjectReferences`, before `CoreCompile` and `BeforeCompile`      | Generates every client that is out of date and adds the generated code to the compilation. A design-time build only adds what an earlier build generated. Hook `AfterTargets` on it to run something after the clients are generated. |
| `ChirographBeforeGenerateOpenApiClients` | first thing `ChirographGenerateOpenApiClients` does, not in a design-time build | Empty. Hook `BeforeTargets` on it to run something before any document is checked, read or downloaded: a target that writes the document a client is generated from, say.                                                             |

A target hooked `BeforeTargets="ChirographGenerateOpenApiClients"` runs too late for that: MSBuild runs a target’s `DependsOnTargets`, where Chirograph does its work, before the targets that are `BeforeTargets` of it. Hook `ChirographBeforeGenerateOpenApiClients` instead, or add the target to `ChirographGenerateOpenApiClientsDependsOn`:

```xml
<Target Name="ExportApiSpec" BeforeTargets="ChirographBeforeGenerateOpenApiClients">
  <Exec Command="dotnet run --project ../Exporter -- $(MSBuildProjectDirectory)/openapi.json" />
</Target>
```

These two targets are the only public ones. The others start with `_Chirograph` and can change in any release.
